items.grounds: Filed ground re-derived from bytes: the row's whole front-seam driver quotes וּבָנוּ֙ חָרְב֣וֹת עוֹלָ֔ם (oshb:Isa.61.4, byte tier), matching “They will rebuild the old ruins.” (web:Isa.61.4), and its boundary_evidence_refs carry neither oshb:Isa.61.3 nor web:Isa.61.3; MT 61:3 closes on וְקֹרָ֤א לָהֶם֙ אֵילֵ֣י הַצֶּ֔דֶק מַטַּ֥ע יְהוָ֖ה לְהִתְפָּאֵֽר (oshb:Isa.61.3, byte tier), matching “that they may be called trees of righteousness, the planting of Yahweh, that he may be glorified.” (web:Isa.61.3), so the finite waw-plus-perfect third-person construction the row names stands on both sides of the seam and discriminates nothing, exactly as filed. The finding's remaining ground ('no vocative, imperative onset, messenger frame, wayyiqtol onset or addressee change stands at MT 61:4') was onset-only, so per the re-adjudication instruction the seam was re-ruled on the complete both-sides test. Side (a), the row's own first verse: וּבָנוּ֙ חָרְב֣וֹת עוֹלָ֔ם שֹׁמְמ֥וֹת רִֽאשֹׁנִ֖ים יְקוֹמֵ֑מוּ וְחִדְּשׁוּ֙ עָ֣רֵי חֹ֔רֶב שֹׁמְמ֖וֹת דּ֥וֹר וָדֽוֹר (oshb:Isa.61.4, byte tier) carries no vocative, no imperative, no divine-speech, massa or hoy frame (the device inventory's koh-amar 48-verse, neum 23-verse, amar-YHWH-adjacency 52-verse, massa and hoy censuses key 0 sites in MT ch 61), and no addressee shift, the unit's second-person-plural address first appearing at צֹאנְכֶ֑ם (oshb:Isa.61.5, byte tier) and וְאַתֶּ֗ם כֹּהֲנֵ֤י יְהוָה֙ תִּקָּרֵ֔אוּ (oshb:Isa.61.6, byte tier): no ruled tier-1 onset. Side (b), the preceding unit's last verse, weighed under the refrain-close rule: 61:3's closing word לְהִתְפָּאֵֽר (oshb:Isa.61.3, byte tier) byte-recurs at exactly one other site, לְהִתְפָּאֵֽר (oshb:Isa.60.21, byte tier; sweep: 2 verses book-wide on the pointed form), where it closes a verse inside the preceding unit rather than that unit's close, which falls at 60:22 on the divine self-identification אֲנִ֥י יְהוָ֖ה (oshb:Isa.60.22, byte tier); and its paired planting noun is not byte-shared, the 60:21 ketiv/qere pair נֵ֧צֶר מטעו מַטָּעַ֛י (oshb:Isa.60.21, byte tier; a K/Q verse in the inventory, checked before slicing) meeting 61:3's מַטַּ֥ע יְהוָ֖ה (oshb:Isa.61.3, byte tier) only at skeleton tier (sweep: 3 verses on that consonantal string, 14:19 included). One non-terminal recurrence with a tier-mixed partner shows no bracket function, so 'refrains close units' does not warrant 61:3 as a close, and no closing formula stands there (neum and amar-YHWH censuses: 0 sites in MT ch 61). Result of the complete test: no ruled tier-1 signal on either side of 61:3|61:4. The seam's only available warrant is the frame-scope close the finding's repair names, and the bytes support it at verse granularity with a qualification the repair must carry: the first-person commission opens at ר֛וּחַ אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִ֖ה עָלָ֑י (oshb:Isa.61.1, byte tier) with אֹתִ֜י and שְׁלָחַ֨נִי֙ (oshb:Isa.61.1, byte tier); its purpose-infinitive chain runs through לָשׂ֣וּם and לָתֵת֩ לָהֶ֨ם (oshb:Isa.61.3, byte tier); the turn to the waw-plus-perfect result chain happens inside 61:3 at וְקֹרָ֤א לָהֶם֙ (oshb:Isa.61.3, byte tier); and וּבָנוּ֙ חָרְב֣וֹת עוֹלָ֔ם (oshb:Isa.61.4, byte tier) continues that chain with an unexpressed third-person-plural subject whose nearest antecedent is 61:3's own plural pronoun (whole-token consonantal count of that pronoun in MT 61:1-9: 4 tokens, 61:3 twice, 61:7 לָהֶֽם and 61:8 אֶכְר֥וֹת לָהֶֽם, byte tier, none in 61:1-2). So 61:3|61:4 is the first verse boundary after the frame's governed chain is exhausted, and no clause spans it: 61:3 ends a complete clause closed by its own purpose infinitive, so the one-sentence rule (a syntactically continuous sentence spanning verses is one unit) does not bind, and 61:4 opens a new clause with its own object. The replacement warrant therefore passes the discrimination test that killed the original only when stated as a frame-scope close, never as a construction contrast, and it must disclose the cross-seam continuity it survives: the waw-plus-perfect chain and the plural referent run across the seam; the first-person-plural לֵאלֹהֵ֑ינוּ (oshb:Isa.61.2, byte tier) recurs as אֱלֹהֵ֔ינוּ (oshb:Isa.61.6, byte tier; sweep: 14 verses book-wide on the consonantal string, these two the only chapter-61 sites), placing the speaker's self-inclusive voice on both sides; and the first person at כִּ֣י אֲנִ֤י יְהוָה֙ (oshb:Isa.61.8, byte tier; וְנָתַתִּ֤י, אֶכְר֥וֹת לָהֶֽם) is YHWH's own voice, a distinct object from the anointed speaker's (the self-identification's consonantal string: sweep 22 verses, 60:22 and 61:8 included; the 61:8 pointed form byte-recurs in 9 verses). Tier-3, single witness: SAMEKH keyed at 60:22 and 61:9, a count-only paseq at 61:3, no seg at 61:4; absence is never counterevidence and nothing in that layer drives this ruling; the sentence break the translation prints before “They will rebuild the old ruins.” (web:Isa.61.4) is translation punctuation and drives nothing. Prior adjudication: it confirmed medium on the frame-scope ground without running the refrain-close test on 61:3; the complete test returns the same outcome, so the verdict is unchanged, but its 'nothing in 61:4-61:9 resumes that voice' needs the qualifications above (the shared plural referent and the first-person-plural form on both sides). Governing rule: a front seam is warranted by a ruled tier-1 onset in the row's first verse or a ruled tier-1 close, refrain-close under the strategy, in the preceding unit's last verse; neither is present, and the seam survives on a frame-scope close the row never states: a warrant defect, not a disclosure gap (low) and not an unwarranted seam (high), because the frame-scope close is byte-supportable at verse granularity and the row's rear seam at 61:10, שׂ֧וֹשׂ אָשִׂ֣ישׂ בַּֽיהוָ֗ה (oshb:Isa.61.10, byte tier, a new first-person voice), is untouched. Confirm at the filed medium; the field repair stands with no seam movement: state the frame-scope close against MT 61:3's bytes, add oshb:Isa.61.3 and web:Isa.61.3 to boundary_evidence_refs, re-cut rejected_alternative to the rival the bytes actually pose (61:4-61:9 read as the continuation of the commission speech of 61:1-61:3, grounded in the shared waw-plus-perfect chain and plural referent), and treat observed_substrate_signals and confidence as dependent fields. Coherence with the preceding row's side of the same seam: its 'changed subject' reason is not byte-discriminating either, since 61:4 names no new subject, so the pair's shared seam rests on the one frame-scope close and both rows' repairs are one edit.
